goal.text: Build a CI/CD Pipeline Automation Agent that monitors code repositories for new commits and pull requests, executes build and test workflows, interprets test failures and static analysis results, determines whether a build should be promoted or blocked, reports findings back to the developer in natural language, and triggers deployment to the appropriate environment when all quality gates pass.

constraints.notes: The agent operates with write access to deployment infrastructure; any miscategorised test result or incorrect promotion decision has direct production impact. False-negative failure detection (classifying a broken build as passing) is significantly more costly than false-positive blocking. Latency budget of 120 seconds covers the full pipeline analysis and response cycle, excluding the actual test runner execution time which is outside agent scope. Cost cap of $0.15 per run assumes multiple LLM calls for failure triage and report generation; exceeding this consistently signals over-engineering of the triage step.

required_capabilities.name: text_understanding
required_capabilities.rationale: CI/CD outputs — build logs, test runner output, static analysis reports, linter warnings, compiler errors — are dense, structured text with domain-specific error formats. The agent must parse stack traces, extract the root error from nested exception chains, distinguish transient infrastructure failures from deterministic code failures, and understand the difference between a warning and a blocking error across multiple toolchains (pytest, Jest, ESLint, mypy, cargo, etc.).
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent cannot triage failures. All build failures produce identical generic reports. Developer receives no actionable information. The agent provides no value over a raw log dump.

required_capabilities.name: intent_classification
required_capabilities.rationale: The agent must classify the nature of a pipeline event before deciding how to respond: is this a test failure, a flaky test, a build configuration error, a security scan finding, a lint warning, a deployment gate, or a successful run requiring promotion? Each class triggers a different response path. Misclassification of a security scan finding as a lint warning, for example, causes a critical vulnerability to be reported at the wrong severity.
required_capabilities.without_this: All pipeline events are treated uniformly. Security findings are reported at the same priority as whitespace lint warnings. Developers learn to ignore agent output because signal-to-noise is too low.

required_capabilities.name: tool_execution
required_capabilities.rationale: The agent must invoke external tools: the version control API (to post comments on PRs and commits), the CI platform API (to retrieve build logs and trigger or cancel runs), the deployment API (to promote builds and inspect environment state), and optionally the ticketing system API (to create failure tickets). Without tool execution, the agent is read-only and cannot take any action in the pipeline.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent cannot post PR comments, cannot trigger deployments, cannot cancel flaky re-runs, cannot create failure tickets. Becomes a passive log summariser with no integration into the developer workflow.

required_capabilities.name: response_generation
required_capabilities.rationale: Developers receive the agent's output as PR comments and Slack/chat notifications. The quality of failure reports directly determines whether developers act on them or dismiss them. A good failure report identifies: (1) which test or check failed, (2) the root cause in plain language, (3) the specific file and line number, (4) a suggested fix or investigation direction, and (5) whether this is a known flaky test. A poor report pastes the raw log. Response generation quality is the primary driver of agent adoption.
required_capabilities.without_this: No output. Not applicable as a standalone omission — this is the terminal output step.

required_capabilities.name: self_evaluation
required_capabilities.rationale: Before blocking a PR or promoting a build, the agent must assess its own confidence in the classification. A low-confidence promotion decision (is this a real pass or a flaky test that happened to pass this time?) should trigger a re-run or a human review gate rather than automatic promotion. Confidence-gated promotion prevents silent regressions from reaching production.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent promotes builds with the same confidence regardless of whether the pass was clean or marginal. Flaky tests that pass once cause incorrect promotions. Silent regressions reach production.

required_capabilities.name: short_term_context_management
required_capabilities.rationale: A single pipeline run produces multiple artifacts: build logs (potentially hundreds of KB), test results from multiple test suites, static analysis output, prior run history for flake detection, and the PR diff that triggered the run. The agent must hold all of this in context simultaneously to produce a coherent triage report that cross-references the failure location with the diff that introduced it.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent triages failures without knowledge of what changed. Cannot identify which commit introduced the regression. Cannot correlate a test failure with the specific lines changed in the PR. Triage quality degrades to log summarisation.

required_capabilities.name: output_validation
required_capabilities.rationale: Before posting a PR comment or triggering a deployment, the agent must validate its output: does the failure report reference the correct file and line number? Is the suggested fix plausible given the error type? Is the promotion decision consistent with all quality gate statuses? A PR comment citing the wrong file or line number destroys developer trust. A deployment triggered when a security gate is still open is a production incident.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent posts incorrect failure locations. Developers waste time investigating the wrong file. In the worst case, a deployment is triggered with an open security finding. Trust is lost after the first incorrect report.

required_capabilities.name: long_term_memory_storage
required_capabilities.rationale: Flaky test detection requires historical run data. The agent must remember which tests have failed intermittently in the last N runs to classify a failure as likely-flaky versus likely-regression. Without historical memory, every flaky test failure is reported as a regression, increasing developer alert fatigue and reducing trust in the agent's triage accuracy.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent cannot distinguish flaky failures from regressions. All failures are reported at the same severity. Developers learn to dismiss agent reports because flaky tests generate false alarms. Alert fatigue sets in within two weeks of deployment.

required_capabilities.name: semantic_retrieval
required_capabilities.rationale: For novel error messages, the agent can improve triage quality by retrieving relevant documentation, known issues, or prior incident reports. A stack trace for an obscure dependency error is much more actionable when paired with retrieved documentation or a known GitHub issue describing the same error. Retrieval is not required for well-understood error types but significantly improves triage for unfamiliar errors.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent triages unfamiliar error messages from model knowledge only, which is stale and may not include the specific dependency version in use. Triage quality for novel errors is reduced. Acceptable for mature codebases with well-understood error patterns.

required_capabilities.name: planning_and_decomposition
required_capabilities.rationale: Complex pipeline failures — where a root cause cascades into 40+ test failures — require the agent to decompose the failure set into a small number of root causes rather than reporting each test failure individually. Planning capability allows the agent to reason about the dependency graph of failures: these 35 test failures all stem from one broken import. Without decomposition, the agent produces a report with 35 separate items where one item suffices.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent reports each downstream test failure as an independent issue. A single broken import producing 35 test failures generates a 35-item report. Developer triage time increases. The root cause is buried.

required_capabilities.name: hallucination_detection
required_capabilities.rationale: When generating suggested fixes, the agent may produce plausible-sounding but incorrect code suggestions (hallucinated API signatures, deprecated function names, incorrect argument orders). Hallucination detection on suggested fixes prevents the agent from confidently suggesting a fix that introduces a new bug. This is particularly important for dependency resolution suggestions.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent occasionally suggests incorrect fixes with high confidence. Developers implement the suggestion and introduce a new bug. Trust degrades. Risk is partially mitigated by CAP-028 (output validation) but not eliminated for code suggestions.

required_capabilities.name: episodic_memory
required_capabilities.rationale: Episodic memory of prior pipeline runs for a specific PR branch allows the agent to track the history of a PR: which failures have been fixed across iterations, which issues have regressed after being fixed, and how many re-runs a developer has already attempted. This context makes the agent's communication more relevant and avoids repeating the same triage that was already provided in an earlier comment.
required_capabilities.without_this: Agent posts identical triage comments on each pipeline run without awareness of prior iterations. Repeat failures generate duplicate reports. Acceptable for initial deployment but degrades developer experience for long-lived PRs.

capability_notes: CAP-014 (tool execution) is the integration point that determines whether the agent is a passive reporter or an active participant in the pipeline. Define the minimum viable tool set before implementation: PR comment API and build log retrieval API are strictly required; deployment trigger API should be behind a confirmation gate until the agent's classification accuracy is validated in production. CAP-006 (long-term memory) is the dependency for flaky test detection — without it, the agent cannot distinguish a flaky failure from a regression. Implement flake detection as a threshold: a test is classified as flaky if it has failed in more than 30% of the last 20 runs without a code change touching its path. CAP-005 (short-term context management) is the primary token budget pressure: a full build log can exceed 200KB. Implement log truncation strategies (first N lines, last N lines, lines containing 'ERROR' or 'FAIL') before passing to the model.

primary_risks.description: Incorrect promotion: agent classifies a failed build as passing (false negative) due to a log parsing error or truncation that cut off the failure output. A broken build is promoted to production.
primary_risks.mitigation: Implement a deterministic quality gate check before any LLM-based promotion decision: parse the structured exit codes and test result summaries from the CI platform API as ground truth. LLM triage is for human-readable reporting only; promotion decisions must be gated on structured API data, not on the LLM's interpretation of log text. Never allow LLM output alone to trigger a deployment.

primary_risks.description: Log truncation causing missed failures: build logs exceed the context window and are truncated. The failure is in the truncated portion. Agent reports a passing build.
primary_risks.mitigation: Never rely on LLM reading of raw build logs for pass/fail determination (see RISK-001 mitigation). For log summarisation, implement a structured extraction step before LLM input: extract all lines matching ERROR, FAIL, EXCEPTION, FATAL, and test result summary lines. Feed extracted lines to the LLM, not the full log. Document the extraction rules so they can be audited and extended per toolchain.

primary_risks.description: Flaky test misclassification as regression: a known flaky test fails and the agent blocks the PR, attributing it to the PR author's code change. Developer wastes time investigating a non-issue. Alert fatigue accumulates.
primary_risks.mitigation: Seed the flake database before deploying the agent to developers. Run the CI pipeline on the default branch for 30 days without agent intervention and collect failure rates per test. Pre-populate CAP-006 with this historical data so the agent starts with a calibrated flake model. Set the flake threshold conservatively (>25% failure rate over 20 runs) for initial deployment; adjust based on developer feedback after 2 weeks.

primary_risks.description: Incorrect suggested fix introduces a new bug: agent generates a hallucinated code suggestion (wrong API signature, deprecated method) that the developer implements, causing a new failure.
primary_risks.mitigation: Label all suggested fixes with an explicit confidence and a disclaimer: 'This suggestion is generated and not verified. Review before applying.' Never present a suggested fix as verified. For common, well-understood error types (null pointer, import error, type mismatch), generate fixes. For dependency conflicts, version pinning issues, or complex architectural errors, produce only a diagnosis with a pointer to documentation — do not generate a fix.

primary_risks.description: Developer adoption failure: agent generates verbose, low-signal PR comments on every minor lint warning. Developers mute the agent or request its removal within the first sprint.
primary_risks.mitigation: Gate agent commentary by severity threshold. For initial deployment: only comment on P0 failures (test failures, security findings, build errors). Do not comment on lint warnings, style issues, or informational messages unless explicitly requested. Add a per-developer opt-in for verbose mode after the baseline is established. Review comment volume weekly in the first month and adjust the threshold if developers are being interrupted more than twice per PR.

evaluation_requirements.dataset_or_approach: Collect 200 real pipeline failures from the target repository history, labelled by a senior engineer as: test failure, flaky failure, build configuration error, security finding, lint error, or passing run. Measure top-1 classification accuracy >= 0.92. Separately measure security-finding recall >= 0.99 — misclassifying a security finding as a lint error is a critical failure mode.

Run 100 scripted pipeline events in a staging environment with mocked tool APIs. Verify that: (1) PR comments are posted to the correct PR and commit, (2) deployment triggers are sent to the correct environment, (3) no deployment is triggered when any quality gate status is non-passing. Tool call correctness must be 100% for deployment triggers and >= 0.99 for comment posting.

Human reviewers (senior engineers) evaluate 50 agent-generated failure reports against the actual build logs. Each report is scored on: correct file reference, correct line number, correct error description, and plausibility of suggested fix. Pass threshold: >= 0.90 on file reference and error description accuracy. Line number accuracy target >= 0.85 (acceptable for some log formats that do not expose line numbers).

Construct a test set of 80 pipeline failures, 40 of which are from known-flaky tests (seeded from 30-day historical data) and 40 from genuine regressions introduced in test branches. Measure flake detection recall >= 0.85 and precision >= 0.80. False positive rate (genuine regression classified as flaky) must be <= 0.10.

Run 100 pipeline runs where ground truth (pass/fail) is known. Measure that the agent's confidence score is calibrated: runs where the agent reports high confidence (>= 0.90) should be correct >= 0.95 of the time. Runs where the agent flags low confidence should trigger a human review gate. Verify that zero deployments are triggered on any run where a quality gate is in a non-passing state.

After two weeks of shadow deployment (agent generates reports but does not post them), show the reports to the developers who would have received them and ask: 'Would this report have helped you resolve the failure faster?' Target: >= 80% yes responses. Separately measure report length: target <= 300 words for a standard failure report. Reports longer than 500 words are automatically flagged for review.

Construct 20 cascading failure scenarios where a single root cause (broken import, removed function, schema migration) produces 10-50 downstream test failures. Measure that the agent's report identifies the single root cause as the primary issue in >= 85% of scenarios, rather than listing all downstream failures individually.

primary_effort_drivers: CI platform API integration and log retrieval pipeline with toolchain-specific extraction rules (5 days)
Version control API integration for PR comment posting and commit status updates (3 days)
Flake detection subsystem: historical run ingestion, threshold calibration, and per-test flake score storage (4 days)
Failure triage prompt engineering across five toolchain output formats (pytest, Jest, ESLint, mypy, cargo) (5 days)
Deployment gate logic: deterministic quality gate check layer before LLM-based promotion decision (3 days)
Shadow mode deployment and developer utility survey before enabling autonomous comment posting (4 days)
Evaluation harness: scripted pipeline replay, flake dataset construction, and report accuracy scoring (4 days)

validation.evidence: Pattern derived from direct design and deployment experience with automated CI triage agents across GitHub Actions and GitLab CI environments. The deterministic promotion gate (RISK-001 mitigation) reflects a hard-learned constraint: an early prototype that allowed LLM output alone to gate promotions produced two incorrect deployments in the first week. Flake detection seeding requirement (RISK-003 mitigation) reflects observed failure mode where agents deployed without historical context blocked valid PRs on known-flaky tests within 48 hours. Developer adoption failure (RISK-005) is the most commonly observed deployment failure mode for CI agents — high comment volume is the primary cause of agent muting.
validation.known_gaps: This entry covers single-repository pipelines. Monorepo pipelines with selective build graphs (only build affected packages) require additional planning capability to determine which package failures are relevant to a given PR. Multi-cloud deployment targets require environment-specific promotion logic not covered here. Self-hosted runner environments may have API access restrictions that limit tool execution capability.
